profiles.meeting_scenario: The meeting is a planning session in an ML research group preparing a two-week internal replication-and-extension sprint based on a paper about using a weighted k-medoids-style formulation to design an assortment of shipping box sizes for a large eCommerce fulfillment network. The team wants to reproduce the paper's core result on Walmart-style fulfillment data available through an internal warehouse simulation environment, then package the outcome into a short research memo and slides for a logistics science review. The agenda is to decide what workstream each person owns, what counts as a usable replication, how the first experiment batch will be run, and when intermediate outputs are due. The expected outcome is a shared plan for the experiment setup, evaluation package, responsibilities, and timeline for the sprint.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: combinatorial optimization, prescriptive ML, offline experiment design
members.background: Maya leads applied ML studies in operations research and has recently been pushing the group to produce fast internal replications before investing in larger-scale engineering work.
members.private_state: She wants a credible replication quickly so she can secure approval for a larger follow-on project, and she is trying to keep the scope narrow enough that the work can be completed with minimal dependence on infrastructure teams.
hidden_assumptions: A 'replication' means recovering the headline directional finding on one representative fulfillment region with a compact experiment bundle, not recreating every operational detail from the original deployment context.

The 'candidate box set' is the already-filtered library of about 1,200 feasible carton dimensions from the internal simulator, because feasibility screening is considered upstream preprocessing rather than part of the study.
A 'sanity-check run' uses the standard research sample covering two weeks of orders from one FC family, because that sample is the lab's normal default for rapid validation.
When they 'report utilization,' a weighted average utilization number plus one or two supporting charts is sufficient for an internal planning memo.
If results are due 'by Friday,' that means a polished artifact in her hands by Friday afternoon Pacific so she can incorporate it into the review deck.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: data pipelines, warehouse simulation systems, experiment orchestration
members.background: Arjun maintains the fulfillment experimentation stack and often translates research ideas into reproducible pipelines that can later be operationalized by product teams.
members.private_state: He wants the work to be structured so it can be reused in the production experimentation framework, and he is wary of analyses that look promising but cannot survive broader operational validation.
hidden_assumptions: A 'replication' means reconstructing the end-to-end study conditions closely enough that another engineer could rerun it later across the full national network without ad hoc researcher-only shortcuts.

The 'candidate box set' includes generating or at least revalidating feasible boxes from the full dimensional catalog before clustering, because feasibility assumptions strongly affect downstream medoid choices.
A 'sanity-check run' means running the standard smoke pipeline on one day of orders across all active FC templates to verify schema, simulator compatibility, and orchestration before scaling up.
When they 'report utilization,' the expected deliverable includes per-node and per-order-family breakdowns, because aggregate averages are not enough to judge operational robustness.
If results are due 'by Friday,' that means the pipeline run should finish by Friday end of day UTC so logs and outputs are available in the shared experiment tracker.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the candidate box set
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'run k-medoids on the candidate box set.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means using the simulator's existing curated list of roughly 1,200 feasible box sizes as the fixed candidate universe.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this includes regenerating or at least re-screening feasible boxes from the broader dimensional catalog before producing the candidate universe used by k-medoids.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see feasibility filtering as obviously part of the background setup, so 'candidate box set' sounds specific enough even though they place the scope boundary in different places.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to do a 'sanity-check run' before the full experiment.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a lightweight research validation on the lab's default two-week sample from one representative FC family to see whether the approach reproduces the expected utilization lift.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a pipeline smoke test on one day of data across all FC templates to verify the experiment machinery, regardless of whether the sample is large enough for meaningful research conclusions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In their group, everyone routinely says 'sanity-check run' for prudent early validation, and each interpretation sounds like the standard obvious first step from that person's role.

misalignment_points.topic: What the results package should contain
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'report utilization results' for the review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes success means a weighted average box utilization improvement number versus the baseline assortment, plus a concise explanation of the methodology.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes success requires breakdowns by FC template, order-size segment, and exception cases so the result can be judged as operationally stable rather than merely positive on average.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both genuinely endorse reporting utilization results, and neither sees their preferred level of granularity as a controversial choice worth surfacing in a short planning meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that results will be ready 'by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes 'by Friday' means she receives a cleaned summary and draft figures by Friday afternoon Pacific in time to use them for her deck.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes 'by Friday' means the pipeline finishes and uploads outputs by Friday end of day UTC, with polishing happening later if needed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadline phrases like 'by Friday' are common shorthand, and because both are trying to be accommodating, neither notices they are anchoring the deadline to different artifacts, time zones, and completion standards.
